meta.build: November 2026 build: 24 CPTAC-3 bulk samples (12 PDAC, 12 adjacent pancreas, 12 patients); healthy reference Baron 2016 (9 cell types); run of 2026-11-09

fields.types: ids of the 13 tumor cell types, in the order of every row of values
fields.typeLabels: plain-language label of each tumor cell type
fields.typeGroups: group of each tumor cell type: malignant, fibroblast (cancer-associated fibroblasts) or other
fields.cells: number of single cells per tumor cell type, summed over the datasets that contribute to its mean
fields.source / definition / caveat: text to show with the values
fields.genes: symbols, in the order of pdac-gene-lookup.json genes, of the tested genes that are measured in the single-cell tumor data; all arrays below follow this order; a tested gene that is absent here is not measured in the tumor data
fields.refMax: per gene, highest share of cells with a count above zero among the 9 healthy reference cell types (3 significant digits); null when the gene is not in the healthy reference
fields.refDetected: per gene, 1 when at least 5% of the cells of at least one healthy reference cell type have a count above zero, else 0 (0 also when the gene is not in the healthy reference)
fields.top: per gene, index into types of the tumor cell type with the highest mean expression; null when all 13 values are 0
fields.fold: per gene, (highest value + 0.01) / (second highest value + 0.01), 3 significant digits
fields.values: per gene, 13 numbers in types order: mean expression in each tumor cell type, counts per 10,000 (not log), 3 significant digits

definitions.values: Counts of each cell are scaled to 10,000. For each tumor cell type the mean is taken within each dataset that has at least 50 cells of the type, then averaged over the datasets.
definitions.cellTypes: malignant = classical and basal-like malignant cells; CAF = the three cancer-associated fibroblast subtypes; mural = pericytes and smooth muscle cells; T/NK = T and NK cells; B/plasma = B and plasma cells; myeloid = macrophages, monocytes, dendritic cells and neutrophils; endocrine = alpha, beta, delta and gamma cells; adipocytes are left out (fewer than 50 cells).
definitions.top: The tumor cell type with the highest mean. Ties are rare; fold near 1 means no cell type stands out.
definitions.refDetected: Uses the healthy pancreas reference of the demo (9 cell types): the share of cells of a type with at least one count of the gene.
definitions.coverage: Every gene tested in the bulk comparison that is measured in the single-cell tumor data (15,304 of 20,221).

sources.tumorSingleCell: Hwang et al., Nature Genetics 2022 (GSE202051, single nuclei); Werba et al., Nature Communications 2023 (GSE205013); Chen et al., Journal of Translational Medicine 2023 (GSE212966)
sources.healthyReference: Baron et al., Cell Systems 2016 (GSE84133), 9 cell types
sources.genes: genes tested in the bulk comparison of this build (see pdac-gene-lookup.json)

source: Hwang et al., Nature Genetics 2022 (GSE202051, single nuclei); Werba et al., Nature Communications 2023 (GSE205013); Chen et al., Journal of Translational Medicine 2023 (GSE212966). Untreated primary tumors; GSE212966 also contributes adjacent pancreas samples.
definition: Counts of each cell are scaled to 10,000. For each tumor cell type the mean is taken within each dataset that has at least 50 cells of the type, then averaged over the datasets.
caveat: These values come from separate public single-cell datasets of other patients, not from the bulk samples of this demo. The single-cell reference is a subsample (at most 1,000 cells per cell state and dataset). Ductal cells from tumors that were not called malignant may include unrecognized malignant cells. The highest cell type is the highest mean; it does not mean the gene is absent from the other cell types.
